subject: MSA term language — auto-renew, notice windows, termination for convenience
messages:
From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>

Cc: Bethany Ross <bethany.ross@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA: Term, auto-renew and termination for convenience — questions

Hi Jonas,

We're reviewing the MSA and have a couple of items procurement flagged around term/renewal mechanics:

- Auto-renew: our procurement team prefers a 60-day explicit notice window to opt out before renewal.
- Termination for convenience: the current draft references a "termination fee" but doesn't define how it's calculated. We need clarity on whether Redwood charges a pro-rata refund, an early termination charge (X months), or waives for pilots.

Attached is our latest term sheet for context (ACME-TermSheet-v3.pdf). Can you share Redwood's standard language and any flexibility for pilot engagements (< $50k ARR)?

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Li
Sr. Procurement Manager, ACME Corp

Subject: Re: MSA: Term, auto-renew and termination for convenience — questions

Thanks for the clear note, Samantha — good questions. Quick summary from our side and next steps: 

1) Auto-renew notice: Redwood's default is a 60-day notice before the end of term for enterprise MSAs. We can make exceptions for pilot/POCs (see below).

2) Termination for convenience: we typically offer two commercial tracks:
   - Enterprise commitments: termination fee = 3 months of committed monthly spend (applies if customer cancels within the committed period).
   - Pilots/POCs: we can waive the termination fee or offer pro-rated refunds for deals under a threshold.

3) Operational handoff: we propose adding a defined 30-day data/export handoff SLA into the MSA so both sides have clear obligations.

I've attached an initial redline that highlights optional language for pilot exemptions and an alternate notice window (ACME_MSA_Redline_v1.docx). Karthik — can you review the suggested legal language below and propose a defendable compromise?

Proposed compromise (commercial): 45-day notice for mid-market deals, 60-day for enterprise; pilots < $25k TCV get 30-day notice and no termination fee.

Next steps: Karthik to provide legal redline; if we can align commercially we will prepare a DocuSign packet.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA: Term, auto-renew and termination for convenience — questions

Jonas / Laura —

Reviewing the draft redline. High-level legal take and recommended changes below (put in redline and comments in the doc):

- Notice window: our preferred standard is 60 days. It's defensible operationally and aligns with our billing cadence. If we offer 45 days as a concession, we should limit it to non-enterprise pilot customers and tag it to a TCV cap.

- Termination for convenience: avoid vague terms. I propose two defined options we can set by exhibit:
   a) No-fee exit (Pilot Exhibit) — applies where total contracted value < $25,000; Customer may terminate with 30 days' notice and Redwood will pro-rate any prepaid amounts and provide data export.
   b) Standard termination (MSA) — Customer may terminate with 60 days' notice and will pay an early termination fee equal to the greater of (i) three months of average monthly committed spend or (ii) any unused committed fees.

- Auto-renew: add explicit opt-out mechanics that tie to invoice/billing cycle; require notice to the designated billing contact and not just contract counsel to prevent missed opt-outs.

- Operational obligations: add a short "sunset and handoff" section: export format, authentication handover, and performance support for 30 days post-termination at no charge for pilots (enterprise to be priced).

I'll push a clean redline incorporating this language to the shared HubSpot record and link the DocuSign template. If ACME needs a 60-day procurement minimum, we can accept that for enterprise, but ask for the pilot carve-out in writing.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Samantha — thanks for the heads up. From a commercial standpoint, asking procurement for flexibility on pilots has worked well when we trade it for a modest concession. Proposed commercial compromise: 

- Enterprise deals: 60-day notice, standard termination fee (3 months committed spend).
- Pilots/POCs under $50k TCV: 30-day notice and waiver of termination fee, provided the pilot is marked in the Order Form and limited to a single 90-day pilot period.
- For mid-market deals ($50k - $200k TCV): 45-day notice and 1-month termination fee.

Also proposing a "sunrise" clause for price changes: if we intend to increase pricing at renewal, we give an early notice of 30 days before the 60-day opt-out window so customers have clarity.

If that sounds workable to you and procurement, we'll have Karthik reflect the language in the redline and circulate a final for signature. Adding pricing-exception-matrix.xlsx for internal reference.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Laura / Jonas — useful options. A couple of clarifications from procurement: 

- Procurement's baseline is 60 days for the auto-renew opt-out. They are open to pilot exceptions but want waivers documented and limited in the Order Form.
- Procurement asks that pilots be allowed to exit without a termination fee (their preference), but business stakeholders want a short operational handoff guarantee (30 days) for knowledge transfer.

Could Redwood confirm: if we mark the engagement as a "pilot" on the Order Form and TCV is under $25k (ACME's pilot size), Redwood will:
  1) Allow 30-day notice for termination;
  2) Waive termination fee; and
  3) Provide a 30-day data handoff + read-only access period for exports.

If you can confirm in writing, procurement can approve the pilot structure and proceed to legal redlines.

Best,
Samantha

Samantha — thanks, and appreciate procurement's clarity. Confirming Redwood's binding commercial/legal approach we can accept for ACME's proposed pilot: 

1) If the engagement is designated as a "Pilot Exhibit" on the Order Form and the total contracted value for the pilot is < $25,000, Redwood will: 
   - Permit termination for convenience with 30 days' written notice;
   - Waive any early termination fee for the pilot period; and
   - Provide a 30-day data export/handoff window and read-only access for an additional 30 days for exports.

2) Enterprise buys (TCV >= $200,000) will retain the 60-day notice and standard termination fee equal to three months of committed monthly spend.

3) Mid-market (between $25k and $200k) — 45-day notice and 1 month termination fee, as discussed.

Operational notes: we'll add a brief "sunset and handoff" schedule to the MSA with format expectations (S3-compatible export, account deprovisioning timeline) and a named billing contact requirement for opt-out notices.

Next steps: Karthik will finalize the redline reflecting the pilot exhibit language and the three-bucket commercial approach. Once the redline is agreed, we'll route for signatures via DocuSign (link to follow).

I'll attach the ticket references and push the redline into HubSpot.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
